holidays.name: National Peanut Cluster Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate clumps of peanuts bound together in chocolate, caramel, or other sweet coatings. Grab a handful and snack responsibly, or irresponsibly.
holidays.origin: Like many food observances, it comes from the American snack-holiday tradition, popularized by food-day calendars and confectionery fans rather than any official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts are not actually nuts. They are legumes that grow underground, making them cousins of beans and lentils.

holidays.name: National Proofreading Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to catching typos, fixing grammar goofs, and double-checking everything before you hit send. Perfect for anyone who has ever emailed the wrong 'there'.
holidays.origin: Created by Judy Beaver, a teacher and writer, to encourage people to care about accuracy in written communication and to give the humble proofreader a moment in the spotlight.
holidays.funFact: The so-called 'Wicked Bible' of 1631 accidentally omitted the word 'not' from the commandment about adultery, and the printers were fined heavily.

holidays.name: International Women's Day
holidays.description: A global day honoring the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women while calling for gender equality. Celebrations range from marches to flower-giving to quiet reflection.
holidays.origin: Rooted in early 20th-century labor movements, with the first observances in 1911. The United Nations began celebrating it in 1975, and it became an annual global event.
holidays.funFact: In Italy, International Women's Day is celebrated with yellow mimosa flowers, a tradition known as La Festa della Donna.

holidays.name: Be Nice to Newbies Day
holidays.description: A day to be kind, patient, and welcoming to anyone new at something, whether that's a new coworker, a new gamer in your lobby, or a first-timer at the gym.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance from the quirky-holiday circuit, encouraging people to remember what it felt like to be the beginner and to help others get a good start.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists note that the 'curse of knowledge' makes experts forget what it was like not to know something, which is exactly why newbies often get frustrated by veterans.

holidays.name: Girl Scout Day
holidays.description: A day when Girl Scouts and fans celebrate the organization's history, from earning badges to selling cookies, with special events and community service projects.
holidays.origin: Commemorates the March 12, 1912 founding of the Girl Scouts of the USA by Juliette Gordon Low in Savannah, Georgia, with celebrations taking place around early-to-mid March.
holidays.funFact: Girl Scout cookies have been sold in some form since 1917, when a troop in Muskogee, Oklahoma, sold homemade cookies in their high school cafeteria.
